body:
Jason is a worldbuilding creative project director, experience producer, creative technologist, and business strategist based across Atlanta, New York, Seattle, Austin, and Los Angeles. He specializes in steering complex, multi-phase media productions through to successful launch — leading cross-functional expert teams through engagements for some of the world's most prominent brands, organizations, and institutions. 

Bildungsromans are key in the Chthulucene, after all.

He currently offers executive creative and technical consulting across immersive, interactive, experiential, entertainment, attraction, and live production — pushing innovation at the convergence of media, arts, and communication technologies with fluency across all producorial forms.

Select clients include Alphabet (Google ATAP, Jigsaw, Chrome, Creative Lab, Maps, YouTube), Meta (Reality Labs, Instagram, Facebook, Oculus), Sonos, Microsoft, General Motors, Spotify, SXSW, Nike, Netflix, Universal, Marvel, the New York City Ballet, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation, Lancôme, Pepsi-Co, Equinox, Levi's, and the Van Alen Institute, among others.

Jason holds an MS in Fiction and Entertainment from SCI-Arc, where he directed a durational immersive transmedia cinematic experience via virtual production — imminently arriving. His MPS from NYU Tisch ITP centered on a speculative critical design concept: a foundry producing luxury survival wares for those navigating the juncture of technocratic urbanity and climate doom. 

His BA from Sarah Lawrence College dual-concentrated in permutative outcomes of Science, Technology & Society, and Material Cultures of Sub-Saharan African cities — where he co-founded the Agent Agitateur Video Collective, stewarded Dominique Malaquais' Right2Fight Symposium, and contributed to activating Donna Haraway's treatises through real-world kinesis.

Beyond client work, Jason facilitates public, community-based innovation programs on behalf of the Queer Underground Hi-Speed Railways Continuum. In 2018, he conceived and produced the Death by Audio Arcade Residency — a queer safe space fused with a DIY tech collective, culminating in the Dreamboxxx: a system of nine original games anchored by a durational symposium.

At the center of it all live the three questions of Gauguin's masterpiece: 

Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? 

His answer: our collaborations are how we get there.

He's just getting started.
